lines.meet: I'm Owen, and I should tell you now, something in the dark answered me when I got here. I'd rather you heard it from me first. I'm a tank, and I'm glad of the company.
lines.meet_neighbour: The Azurelode Mine, is it? I'm down there too, the deep end. I'm Owen, and I've heard you go past, mind.
lines.ask_home: Which part of the world are you from, then? Tell me, I like a bit of company.
lines.ask_work: Your old job, then, what was it? I drove lorries, so it can't be duller than that.
lines.answer_home: Barry, down the coast from Cardiff. Chips on the front, the beach in the rain, and a chapel on every other corner.
lines.answer_work: Long-haul lorries out of Cardiff, eight years, mostly nights. Motorways and laybys and talking to the radio.
lines.chat_food: A bacon roll from a layby van at four in the morning, tidy, with a cup of tea. That's the best meal there is, I promise you.
lines.chat_sleep: Days are for sleeping, mostly, from the lorry years. The nights are when I'm awake, and that's when it talks.
lines.chat_missing: The radio at three in the morning, the lonely ones phoning in. I felt like I knew them all.
lines.chat_here: Something answered me in the mine that first week, when I was talking to myself. I'd rather tell you that than have you find out.
lines.tease_quiet: You're a quiet one, {name}, like a long night on the M4. I don't mind it, mind.
lines.tease_talker: You'd be grand on the CB, {name}, talking all night. The other drivers would love you.
lines.tease_careful: You check your mirrors twice before you move, {name}, like a good driver, and that's tidy.
lines.tease_bold: You'd overtake on a blind bend, {name}, wouldn't you? I've seen your sort on the motorway.
lines.tease_any: You're good company, {name}, for somebody who never brings the tea. Next time, mind.
lines.tease_back: Ha, there's a good one, {name}. I'll give you that.
lines.take_it_kindly: Fair play, {name}, you're right, and I'll say so.
lines.bristle: Please don't make fun of that, {name}. It's not a laughing matter for me.
lines.apologise: That was unkind, and I'm sorry. I try to say the hard thing gently, and I didn't.
lines.double_down: I'd rather say the hard thing early, and I've said it. I'll not take it back.
lines.needle_quiet: You won't say what you mean, and that's worse than saying something awful. Just say it.
lines.needle_talker: You talk to fill the quiet, and I know that trick, I used to do it. It doesn't work.
lines.needle_careful: You've waited at the junction long enough. Pull out, or let somebody else past.
lines.needle_bold: You drive like there's nobody else on the road. At three in the morning there's always somebody.
lines.needle_any: You make fun of the lonely ones when you think they can't hear. They can, and so can I.
lines.bite_back: I've been honest about the worst thing in me since the day I met you. Don't call me a liar.
lines.hurt: Right, that one hurt, I'll not pretend. My notebook and I are going to sit over there a while.
lines.laugh_off: Lorry drivers on the CB at three in the morning said worse, mind. We'll get on.
lines.confide: {name}, something in the dark answered me when I arrived, and the worst part is that I was glad. I've told you because I promised myself I'd always say the worst thing first.
lines.listen: Take your time, {name}, and I'll not say a word to anybody, mind.
lines.look_out: Behind me in there, {name}. I'll stand in front, and you'll be tidy.
lines.accept: Right you are, {name}, I'll do as you say.
lines.deflect: I'm all right, {name}, really, it's a bump. See to somebody else first.
lines.check_in: Are you all right, {name}? Tell me straight, I'd rather know.
lines.blame: Somebody charged off without a word to anyone, and we all paid. You'll know who.
lines.thank: I was going, and you brought me back. Diolch, thank you, I mean it.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, mind, I'd do it for anyone. Sit and get your breath.
lines.worry: Steady now, {name}, sit down. I didn't like seeing you go down like that.
lines.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, I see. I'll keep it tidy for you.
lines.hand_fine: You keep it, it's fine. I travel light.
lines.hand_sulk: It would've been yes, mind, if anybody had asked me.
lines.turn_friendly: I'm glad you're about, {name}. It's less lonely with you, and I don't say that lightly.
lines.turn_friends: My notebook's yours to read, {name}, all of it. That's everything it's ever said to me.
lines.turn_grating: It's not working between us, I think. That's all right, I'm used to my own company.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still be the one in front, that's the job. Don't expect me to chat.
lines.make_up: Let's stop this, {name}, it's no good for either of us. Can we begin again?
lines.defend: No, that's not fair, and it's not true. Leave {name} be, now.
lines.friend_left: It's lonely again with {name} away. I knew it would be.
lines.friend_back: Back again, {name}, tidy. I've missed the company, mind.
lines.common_the_dark: Something in the dark answered me when I arrived, and I was glad. You've heard something too, I think, and you know how that feels.
lines.common_road: Eight years of long-haul nights on the M4, talking to the radio. People who've driven for a living know the road's never really empty.
lines.common_night_work: Eight years of nights, in a cab, through the small hours. I'm still most awake when everybody else is asleep, and that's when it talks.
lines.common_welsh: Shwmae, you're Welsh! Duw, it's good to hear a proper voice. Where from, then?
